tasks.short: Direct and coordinate school teachers, administrators, and support staff

steps.what: Compile staff priorities and open actions
Direct and coordinate school staff activities

tasks.design: A {PROJECT} board assembles existing priorities and turns the administrator's coordination decisions into named actions and reminders. The administrator still directs people and resolves workload conflicts; the board does not allocate staff on its own.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination depends on local knowledge, relationships and competing needs.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared action board removes repeated copying of agreed work between meetings and email.
tasks.still_hard: The administrator must judge trade-offs and intervene when priorities or people conflict.
tasks.human_edge: They can recognise capacity, care and service consequences that an action list cannot settle.

ambition.what: Review cross-team blockers before weekly coordination meetings.

tasks.altitude: The administrator manages patterns of work and blockers rather than compiling updates.

evidence.claim: Shared work records can track actions, owners and due dates.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: priorities assembled through follow-ups sent.
Input contract: action, owner, due date, dependency and status; team leads provide updates; a meeting note is the fallback.
Existing automatic reminders are not counted as labour saved.
Incremental upkeep is 2 hours per 100 baseline hours for board fields and routes.
unknowns: Which staff assignments can be changed by the administrator.
How complete current action updates are.
research_questions: How much meeting time is spent finding status?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: People leadership and conflict resolution stay manual; only status assembly and follow-up handling are reduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and submit budget requests, recommendations, and grant proposals

steps.what: Collect programme costs and funding evidence
Set budget request or grant case
Prepare budget request or grant proposal

loop.input: checked evidence, request assumptions and funder fields
loop.check: Administrator reconciles all figures and claims to the evidence pack before approval.
loop.stop: One draft; missing evidence or figures route to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: The proposal needs case-specific narrative and evidence selection.

steps.what: Approve final proposal version for submission
Submit approved budget or grant proposal

tasks.design: A {DOCS} workspace links cost evidence to a proposal and preserves the exact approved version. The administrator makes the funding case and approves that version; only then may the workflow submit it through {GOV_PORTAL} or {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Funding requests require local priorities, accurate evidence and accountable external commitments.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured evidence fields and versioned documents reduce rekeying and formatting around a proposal.
tasks.still_hard: The administrator must decide the request, substantiate claims and accept responsibility for submission.
tasks.human_edge: They can judge which investment has educational value and defend it to a funder.

ambition.what: Maintain a reusable evidence library for future programme funding proposals.

tasks.altitude: The administrator builds a funding portfolio instead of reconstructing prior evidence each cycle.

evidence.claim: A versioned document workflow can prevent submission of an unapproved draft.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: evidence collected through proposal submitted after version-bound approval.

Input contract: funding source, cost centre, amount, evidence reference, claim, owner and proposal version; finance and programme owners supply fields; a controlled document checklist is the fallback.
The submission action uses only the exact version approved in s4.
Incremental upkeep is 3 hours per 100 baseline hours for funder fields and evidence links.
unknowns: Who may approve each proposal value and funder type.
Whether an external portal accepts a machine-submitted file.
research_questions: How much proposal effort is reconciliation versus argument development?
Which evidence fields are repeatedly missing at review?

already_counted.description: Funding case, proposal review and version approval

incremental.description: Maintain funder fields and evidence links

approvals.approved_version: approved proposal version matching the submitted file

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The funding case and approval stay human; savings apply to evidence assembly, drafting and controlled submission.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and develop instructional methods and content for student programmes

steps.what: Collect learner needs and existing materials
Plan instructional methods for the programme

loop.input: learning sequence and approved source material
loop.check: Administrator tests content against objectives, age and accessibility needs.
loop.stop: One draft; unsuitable content is rewritten manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Instructional content needs free-text creation and pedagogic fit.

steps.what: Pilot activities and revise instructional content

tasks.design: A {DOCS} collection holds the programme brief, source materials, content versions and pilot feedback. The administrator chooses methods, tests activities and validates content; drafting help is bounded to a checked first version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Good instruction depends on learner needs, subject knowledge and practice, not a universal template.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared source collection and structured activity brief reduce repeated searching and formatting.
tasks.still_hard: The administrator must judge pedagogic quality, accessibility and what worked in a real activity.
tasks.human_edge: They can adapt methods to learners and notice when an activity fails despite a plausible plan.

ambition.what: Maintain reusable, tested activity patterns for student programmes.

tasks.altitude: The administrator builds and improves a content system rather than recreating materials from scratch.

evidence.claim: A bounded draft can turn approved source material into a reviewable content first version.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: learner needs collected through pilot feedback recorded.
Input contract: audience, objective, source material, method, activity, accessibility need and pilot feedback; teachers and programme leads supply fields; a manual content brief is the fallback.
Incremental upkeep is 3 hours per 100 baseline hours for source curation and content versioning.
unknowns: Which materials are licensed for reuse.
Which accessibility adaptations are required for each programme.
research_questions: Which content elements are repeatedly revised after a pilot?
How much time is spent locating approved source material?

already_counted.description: Method selection, content review and pilot revision

incremental.description: Curate source material and content versions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Method choice and testing remain human; savings are in assembling sources and producing a reviewable first content draft.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach classes or courses to students

steps.what: Prepare class resources and attendance list
Teach class or course to students

tasks.design: The {LMS} prepares the class pack and holds attendance and follow-up notes. Teaching and real-time assessment stay with the administrator; no model speaks to, scores or directs students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teaching depends on live attention, trust and response to individual learners.
tasks.enabler_now: Resource assembly and basic lesson records can be configured around the class without changing the teaching.
tasks.still_hard: The administrator must see misunderstanding, adjust explanation and care for the group.
tasks.human_edge: They build a learning relationship and respond safely to what happens in the room.

ambition.what: Give absent students a consistent follow-up resource pack after each course.

tasks.altitude: The administrator studies participation patterns instead of spending class-adjacent time assembling files and records.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can hold course resources and attendance records.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: class resources prepared through attendance and follow-up recorded.
Input contract: class identifier, lesson date, resource links, attendance state and follow-up note; administrator supplies lesson context; a paper register is the fallback.
Existing automated attendance capture is not counted as new labour saving.
Incremental upkeep is 1 hour per 100 baseline hours for resource metadata.
unknowns: Whether attendance is currently captured manually.
What follow-up material absent students are permitted to receive.
research_questions: How much time is spent preparing the same class resources repeatedly?
Which follow-up resources help students rejoin a course?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Teaching and live assessment remain human; only resource preparation and record entry are reduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The administrator keeps leadership, funding, instructional and teaching judgement while reducing assembly, routing and record work.
reach: Work with finance on evidence-ready funding schedules.
Work with learning coordinators on reusable resource packs.
role.ambitious_version: A school leader who can spend more time on staff, instruction and funding choices because routine coordination is visible and traceable.
